description:
Everyone “knows” inequality is getting worse.
Everyone “knows” it’s one of the biggest problems of our time.
And almost everyone is wrong—at least about why.

In this Econ Nerds episode, we walk through three inequality myths that refuse to die, even as the data keeps contradicting them.

We start with pizza and prehistoric violence, move through global poverty collapses and academic knife fights, and end with a deeply uncomfortable question:

Why did outrage about inequality explode just as inequality stopped rising so fast?

This video isn’t about defending billionaires or claiming everything is fine. It’s about how:
- The world shifted from a zero-sum economy to a growing-pie one
- Billions of people escaped extreme poverty (and why no one talks about it)
- Two research teams can tell wildly different inequality stories based on the exact same data
- Media, incentives, and resentment shape which numbers get amplified
- A frustrated, overeducated elite may be driving today’s inequality panic

If you’ve ever felt like the inequality conversation is missing something, this might be it. Watch with an open mind. Or don’t, and call Matt a bootlicker in the comments. Either way works.

For more details check out our Substack: https://open.substack.com/pub/econnerds/p/3-inequality-myths

And follow us on X for even more Econ Nerdy content: https://x.com/Econ_Nerds
